raw_response:
I’ve been farming these 8 mu for 40 years now. My husband and I are both getting old, just the two of us left on the farm. Our son works in Shijiazhuang and only comes back for holidays. I only went to primary school, but I know this land better than any book. I don’t count kilograms like those young technicians — I know how many bags I need, and I know what the wheat looks like when it’s hungry.

It’s early October now, and the maize is just coming off. I need to get the wheat in the ground by around the 12th — if I wait too long the wheat won’t tiller well before winter. Last year the maize was late because of rain and the wheat suffered, but this year the weather looks normal. I buy improved wheat seed every few years, about 45 yuan per mu. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — that’s my usual amount, about 35 kg. Last year I tried less because fertilizer got expensive, and the wheat turned yellow at jointing. Never again. Better to spend the money than risk losing half the crop. At jointing time in March or April, I topdress with about 20 kg of urea per mu. I irrigate three times: once after planting if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Pumping costs 25 yuan each time, so if it rains I might skip one, but usually I don’t take chances. I spray herbicide in early spring, and if I see aphids I spray for them too — that’s another 25 yuan per mu. For harvest in June I hire the combine and maybe a helper, about 3 days of hired labor total. I expect about 400 kg per mu if the frost doesn’t hit wrong.

The maize goes in right after wheat harvest, around June 15th. The window is tight — sometimes only three or four days. I don’t have time to plow deep, just rotary till and plant. I use hybrid seed, whatever the shop has — usually Zhengdan 958 or something similar. About 55 yuan per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the row at planting, about 30 kg per mu, and when the corn is knee-high I topdress with about 15 kg urea per mu. My neighbor Lao Zhang cut back last year and his corn was shorter than mine, so I’m not changing. I irrigate twice: once at planting if it’s dry, and once at the big trumpet stage. If it’s very dry at silking I might do a third, but twice is usually enough. Herbicide at planting, and maybe insecticide if the corn borers come. I hire help for harvest — about 3 days. I expect about 450 kg per mu.

All together, seeds, fertilizer, water, spray, and hired help will cost me around 5,000 yuan this year. That’s a lot for two old people, but we have a little savings. I worry about prices, but I worry more about a bad harvest. I’d rather apply a bit too much than too little.
